rules.sentence: This form is characterized by mutism, inhibited movement, posturing, negativism, and staring.[30][31] Postures may be mundane (eg, sitting or standing in the same position for hours) or unusual (eg, head raised above the bed as if on a pillow).
Speech, spontaneous movements, and response to voice or noxious stimuli are decreased.
In more severe cases, eating and drinking may cease, and stupor and incontinence may occur.[32]

This subtype is characterized by excessive and purposeless motor activity in the upper and lower extremities (hyperkinesis), restlessness, stereotypy (repetitive movements such as pacing or grimacing), impulsivity (sudden, unpredictable agitation), verbigeration (repetitive, meaningless speech), and paradoxical negativism (doing the opposite of what the examiner asks such as sitting when asked to stand).[30][31]
Delirium may occur in severe cases, and excessive motor activity may lead to self-injury or harm to others.[33]
